To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) NPC1L1 is present in the human enterocyte and is associated with the apical membrane, 2) NPC1L is also localized in the endosome, lysosome, and mitochondria, 3) NPC1L deficiency results in decreased intestinal cholesterol uptake, and 4) NPC1L knockdown causes a decline in SR-BI expression.

NPC1L-1 is localized to apical membrane, endosomes, lysosomes, and mitochondrion of the human enterocyte and that NPC1L deficiency in Caco-2 cell line causes a decrease in cholesterol uptake and a change in the expression of key genes regulating cholesterol homeostasis in enterocytes.

NPC1L is localized in the apical membrane of human enterocytes and its suppression causes an increase in cholesterol absorption and a reduction in cholesterol synthesis and cholesterol esterification in Caco-2 human enterocyte-like cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
defining the molecular mechanism of cholesterol uptake in human enterocytes and its regulation.
defining the role of NPC1-L1 in cholesterol absorption.
defining the role of NPC11L1 in the regulation of intestinal cholesterol uptake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NPC1L is an apical membrane protein of the enterocyte that mediates cholesterol absorption.
NPC1L is an important player in cholesterol absorption, and it is a key regulator in intestinal cholesterol homeostatis.
NPC1L-1 plays a role in cholesterol uptake in human enterocytes.

the NPC1L1 protein is present in human enterocytes and that it plays a role in intestinal cholesterol absorption.

NPC1L is a critical component of the enterocyte for cholesterol absorption in humans.
